source_transcription_validation.canonical_script:
How does the Newman CLI turn manual API clicks into automated infrastructure?
Clicking a test button works locally, but it can't automatically catch breaking bugs when your team pushes new code.
Take a standard Postman collection, designed to verify if a checkout API returns a success status.
The first step is exporting that visual interface into a plain text file.
This preserves every request and assertion exactly as you wrote it.
But testing this automatically means hitting a temporary preview server, not production.
So how does a static file know where to point?
Newman solves this by accepting command line flags that dynamically inject the correct environment URL right at the moment of execution.
It runs the requests headlessly, without a visual interface, and returns a definitive pass or fail code to serve as an automated quality gate before the code merges.
So what exactly happens to that visual checkout collection you originally spent hours building by hand?
Newman transforms it into a permanent pipeline gatekeeper, automatically blocking broken code from reaching production on every single update.
